title: Locker and Tryouts
premise: Odile Vasquez, a scholarship senior at Ashgrove Academy, is counting down the days to graduation when notes signed by the school's legendary ghost begin appearing in her locker — written in ink that shouldn't exist. The notes lead her to evidence that the academy's beloved founder covered up a student's death decades ago, a cover-up that powerful families still protect. As Odile and an unlikely crew of outcasts dig for the truth, loyalty fractures: her best friend's family is implicated, her mentor warns her to stop, and the 'ghost' turns out to be someone she trusts. In the end, Odile chooses truth over safety, exposing the archive before the final spring audition, and finds that the found family she built along the way — not the diploma, not the school's approval — is what she was actually auditioning for.
about_author: Lena Almeida is a former boarding school music scholar who writes stories about the kids institutions overlook. She lives in a coastal town with a rescue greyhound and an unhealthy number of annotated paperbacks.

chapters.title: Day 212
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She maps her remaining days at Ashgrove like a prison sentence, cataloguing rules, scholarship obligations, and the spring audition that could secure her future. Establishes her isolation and her careful invisibility. Beat: weary resignation masking fierce ambition.

chapters.title: The Ink That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Odile finds the first note in her locker, addressed by name, in ink that shimmers and refuses to smudge. No one claims it. She tells no one. Beat: unease sharpening into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter on how Odile learned to survive Ashgrove: be excellent, be quiet, be grateful. Her scholarship sponsor's condescending letter reminds her what she stands to lose. Beat: pressure tightening.

chapters.title: Second Note
chapters.summary: The ghost leaves a second note referencing something Odile said aloud only once, alone. She tests her few suspects, including charming Theo Marsh and sharp-tongued Priya Nair. Beat: paranoia blooming.

chapters.title: The Legend of the Grey Girl
chapters.summary: Priya recounts the campus ghost story — a student who died in the old music hall in 1974, whose name the school quietly erased. Odile realizes the notes quote the legend verbatim. Beat: intrigue deepens into purpose.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Convenience
chapters.summary: Odile and Priya, never friends before, agree to investigate together. They inventory the notes and discover a pattern: dates matching school archive closures. Beat: cautious trust.

chapters.title: Theo at the Door
chapters.summary: Theo catches them sneaking toward the music hall and, instead of reporting them, asks to join. Odile distrusts his motives — his family built half of Ashgrove. Beat: friction and grudging acceptance.

chapters.title: The Sealed Wing
chapters.summary: The trio explores the condemned wing of the music hall, finding a bricked-over practice room and a child's scratched initials: R.M. Beat: dread and wonder.

chapters.title: Third Note, New Tone
chapters.summary: A note arrives warning them to stop — but the handwriting has changed. Someone else is writing now, or the ghost is frightened. Beat: stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: Odile uses her work-study access to reach the restricted archive. She photographs a 1974 enrollment ledger with a page razored out. Beat: first real transgression, exhilarating terror.

chapters.title: The Sponsor's Warning
chapters.summary: Odile's scholarship sponsor, Dean Whitlock, summons her — not about the archive, but a vague warning about 'students who mistake curiosity for entitlement.' Beat: the institution showing its teeth.

chapters.title: Priya's Secret
chapters.summary: Priya admits her aunt was the last person to see the Grey Girl alive and never spoke of it again. Her family has its own wound. Beat: vulnerability, deepening bonds.

chapters.title: The Recital
chapters.summary: A mandatory winter recital forces Odile back into performance mode. Watching Whitlock charm donors, she notices the Marsh family patriarch flinch at the music hall's name. Beat: observation as weapon.

chapters.title: What R.M. Stood For
chapters.summary: The trio identifies R.M. — Rosa Marchetti, a scholarship student, like Odile. The parallel lands hard. Beat: history rhyming with the present.

chapters.title: Break-In Weather
chapters.summary: A storm knocks out campus security. The trio attempts to reach the bricked room's other side through the sub-basement. They find a hidden satchel: Rosa's diary, water-damaged but legible. Beat: triumph shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Rosa's Voice
chapters.summary: Diary excerpts, interwoven with Odile's present: Rosa documented favoritism, cruelty, and a teacher who 'watched too long.' The final entry is dated the night she died. Beat: grief across time.

chapters.title: The Official Story
chapters.summary: School records call Rosa's death an accident during a solo practice. The diary suggests she was meeting someone. Beat: the first hard evidence of a lie.

chapters.title: Theo's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Theo confesses his grandfather was headmaster in 1974 — and that his family's name is all over the era's documents. He's terrified but stays. Beat: loyalty tested by blood.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Odile's locker is emptied, her diary photos gone from her cloud account. The school knows. Beat: safety collapsing.

chapters.title: The Interrogation
chapters.summary: Whitlock questions Odile gently, kindly, offering her a named mentorship and a recommendation letter — if she distances herself from 'troublemakers.' Beat: temptation dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: The Fourth Note
chapters.summary: A note slips into Odile's sheet music during rehearsal: 'They erased her once. Don't let them erase you.' The ink is the impossible ink. The ghost is close. Beat: resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: Narrowing the Circle
chapters.summary: Odile lists who could access her locker, the archive, and rehearsal. The list is short. One name on it guts her. Beat: suspicion turning inward.

chapters.title: The Confession She Didn't Ask For
chapters.summary: Odile confronts the person — elderly caretaker Marisol Dunn, who as a student found Rosa's body and was paid to stay silent. She has been leaving the notes for fifty years. Beat: the ghost is human, and tired.

chapters.title: Marisol's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marisol reveals she kept her own records: payments, threats, the name of the teacher Rosa was meeting. But she wants something before she talks — for Odile to sing Rosa's story at the spring audition, on stage, where the school must listen. Beat: the plan is born.

chapters.title: Rehearsal as Reconnaissance
chapters.summary: Odile prepares her audition piece while the trio maps how to unseal the practice room publicly — during the audition, with donors present. Beat: tension braided with artistry.

chapters.title: Priya Breaks
chapters.summary: Priya's family, threatened by an anonymous caller, orders her to stop. She wavers — loyalty to family versus loyalty to truth. Beat: the cost becomes real.

chapters.title: The Offer Odile Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Whitlock offers Odile a full-ride university placement, contingent on 'discretion.' It's everything she came to Ashgrove for. Beat: the devil's bargain at its most seductive.

chapters.title: What Odile Wants
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: Odile sits with Rosa's diary and admits she's been auditioning for the school's approval her whole life. She decides she'd rather be free than chosen. Beat: the turn.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: The plan fractures: Theo wants to go to his grandfather directly; Priya wants to walk away; Marisol's health is failing. Odile must lead or lose everything. Beat: crisis of the found family.

chapters.title: Day 12
chapters.summary: Twelve days to graduation, seven to the audition. The trio reconciles on their own terms — no one gets to be the hero alone. Beat: repaired and hardened bonds.

chapters.title: Unbricking
chapters.summary: They quietly open the sealed practice room, preserving evidence: Rosa's belongings, a torn letter implicating the teacher — and the Marsh patriarch's signature as a witness to the cover-up. Beat: the trap is set.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: They send copies to a journalist, an alumnae network, and — as insurance — to every senior's email. There's no taking it back. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Whitlock's Countermove
chapters.summary: The school suspends Odile pending 'an honor review,' barring her from the audition. Theo's family threatens to disown him. Beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Marisol's Last Gift
chapters.summary: Marisol, hospitalized, gives Odile the original 1974 incident report she stole decades ago — and tells her the audition rulebook has a clause: any student may perform if nominated by a faculty member in writing. Beat: the door reopens.

chapters.title: The Teacher Who Signs
chapters.summary: A retiring music teacher, Ms. Okonkwo, who has suspected the truth for years, signs the nomination form and dares the administration to stop her. Beat: an adult choosing the kids.

chapters.title: Audition Day
chapters.summary: Odile performs — and mid-piece, speaks Rosa Marchetti's name, telling the room what the school buried while donors, students, and the journalist listen. Beat: the climax; courage as performance.

chapters.title: The Room Where It Happened
chapters.summary: The fallout detonates: the Marsh patriarch resigns from the board, Whitlock is suspended pending investigation, and the practice room is unsealed publicly as a memorial. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered in daylight.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Graduation approaches. Odile is offered reinstatement, honors, apologies — the labels she once craved. She takes the diploma, not the halo, and declines the university placement bought with her silence. Beat: quiet triumph.

chapters.title: Day 0
chapters.summary: Graduation day. Priya, Theo, Marisol in a wheelchair, and Ms. Okonkwo watch Odile cross the stage. The found family poses for a photo where the school's crest is cropped out. Beat: warmth earned.

chapters.title: The Last Note
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Packing her locker one final time, Odile finds a last note in impossible ink: Rosa's real signature, traced by Marisol, with one line — 'Sing it anyway.' Odile smiles, keeps the note, and walks out the front gate. Beat: release, and the story handed forward.
